note: Saved NASA OSDR data (not live). Fact cards are short, simplified summaries.

facts.text: Mice lived on the space station for 37 days. Some of their leg bones got weaker. In space, bones carry less weight.
facts.study_title: 37-Day microgravity exposure in 16-Week female C57BL/6J mice during the NASA Rodent Research 1 mission is associated with bone loss specific to weight-bearing skeletal sites (femur and vertebrae, micro computed tomography)

facts.text: Mice flew on the Space Shuttle for 15 days. Bone in the top of their skulls grew, even though leg bones usually get thinner.
facts.study_title: Fifteen days of microgravity causes growth in calvaria of mice (STS-131)

facts.text: Muscles get weaker in space. Scientists studied muscles of mice from the space station to learn why.
facts.study_title: Spaceflight increases sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ leak and this cannot be counteracted with BuOE treatment (Soleus muscle from RR-18, Western Blot and ATPase Assays)

facts.text: Scientists checked how leg muscles of mice changed after 30 days in orbit.
facts.study_title: Global gene expression analysis highlights microgravity sensitive key genes in soleus and EDL of 30 days space flown mice

facts.text: In one study, a special treatment helped mice keep more muscle and bone during spaceflight.
facts.study_title: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight [plasma proteomics]

facts.text: Four private astronauts flew for 3 days on Inspiration4. Scientists took blood samples before and after to see how bodies react to space.
facts.study_title: SpaceX Inspiration4 Blood Serum Metabolic Panel and Immune/Cardiac Cytokine Arrays (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Multiplex)

facts.text: Scientists tested blood from two astronauts before and after a space trip. Some changes went back to normal after 3 months.
facts.study_title: Longitudinal transcriptomic and epigenetic analysis in astronauts reveals dynamic immune response to spaceflight [RNA-seq]

facts.text: Space can change how the body fights germs. Scientists studied brains of mice that spent 37 days on the space station.
facts.study_title: Effects of Space Flight on Inflammasome Activation in the Brain of Mice (Cortex; ECLIA)

facts.text: Long space trips can affect muscles, bones, the heart and the body's defences. Scientists studied mouse tissues of different ages.
facts.study_title: Spaceflight induces systemic effects on extracellular matrix and immune system in different age-stages - Blood data

facts.text: Astronauts grew and harvested leafy greens on the space station. Scientists tested how light colour changes the plants.
facts.study_title: Pick-and-eat space crop production flight testing on the International Space Station (Elemental Analysis, ORAC, Phenolic Content)

facts.text: Lettuce was grown on the space station. Scientists checked it on Earth to see if it was safe and healthy to eat.
facts.study_title: Microbiological and nutritional analysis of lettuce crops grown on the International Space Station-VEG01B

facts.text: Scientists checked tiny living things called microbes on space-grown salad leaves to make sure the food is safe.
facts.study_title: Spatial characterization of microbial communities on multi-species leafy greens grown simultaneously in the Veggie vegetable production systems on the International Space Station VEG-03D

facts.text: Scientists studied how the leaves of small wheat plants change when they grow in space.
facts.study_title: Microgravity effects on leaf morphology, cell structure, carbon metabolism and mRNA expression of dwarf wheat

facts.text: Plants react to light in space. On the space station, scientists compared plants grown in light and in the dark.
facts.study_title: Light has a principal role in the Arabidopsis transcriptomic response to the spaceflight environment

facts.text: Scientists studied the roots of a small plant called Arabidopsis after it grew on the space station.
facts.study_title: Glycome profiling and immunohistochemistry uncover changes in cell walls of Arabidopsis thaliana roots during spaceflight: Advanced Plant EXperiment (APEX) 03-1 Raw Dataset

facts.text: Space radiation is made of fast, high-energy particles. In lab tests on human cells, it caused damage to DNA, the cell's instruction book.
facts.study_title: Space radiation induces distinct senescent phenotypes: Implications for space travel [scRNA-Seq]

facts.text: Scientists sent seeds on a high-altitude flight over Antarctica to see how cosmic radiation can change them.
facts.study_title: Approaches for Surveying Cosmic Radiation Damage in Large Populations of Arabidopsis thaliana Seeds- an Antarctic Example
